title: Garden and Promise
premise: Rosalind Almeida, a cellist whose career collapsed mid-concert, retreats to her late grandmother's coastal house to sell it — and finds an unopened letter postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to a man named Elias who once loved her grandmother and vanished. As Rosalind searches for the letter's recipient, she collides with Theo, the ferry mechanic who turns out to be Elias's grandson and keeper of his family's side of a decades-old silence. Uncovering what really happened forces Rosalind to confront why her own final performance failed: not her hands, but her refusal to be seen. In the end, she chooses truth over the safe version of herself, plays again at the season's last crossing, and boards the ferry with Theo as the garden her grandmother planted blooms out of season.
about_author: Q. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent a decade cataloguing other people's music before writing about the silences between notes. They live on a cold coastline with a dog named after a tempo marking.

chapters.title: The Broken Bow
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A flashback frames her catastrophic final concert — frozen hands, a snapped bow hair, a hall of pitying faces — then cuts to her arriving at her grandmother's shuttered coastal house, tasked with selling it. Emotional beat: numb avoidance dressed up as practicality; she has come to close a door, not open one.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. While clearing the attic she finds an unopened love letter from 2013, addressed to 'Elias,' in her grandmother's handwriting but never sent — or never delivered. Reading it, she realizes her grandmother had a whole hidden life. Emotional beat: vertigo; the woman she mourned is suddenly a stranger, and Rosalind can't stop reading.

chapters.title: The Man at the Ferry Ramp
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She takes the letter to town and encounters Theo, a blunt, grease-stained ferry mechanic who recognizes the name Elias — it was his grandfather. He is guarded, almost hostile, and warns her some letters stay lost for a reason. Emotional beat: friction and unwanted recognition; he sees through her deflections instantly.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo tends the overgrown garden behind the house, which his grandfather helped plant, and remembers Elias's silence after the summer of 2013. Watching Rosalind struggle with the roses, he softens despite himself. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness; two people grieving different people in the same soil.

chapters.title: Intermission
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A storm strands them together overnight in the boathouse. Rosalind admits her career-ending performance wasn't a hand injury but panic — she couldn't bear being truly seen on stage. Theo tells her Elias stopped writing after one unanswered letter. Emotional beat: mutual confession; intimacy arrives sideways, through damage.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds Elias's unsent reply hidden in the ferry office — proof Elias wrote back, that the silence was a lie someone maintained. He must decide whether to show Rosalind, knowing it will shatter her image of her grandmother. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth made literal; he chooses truth and hates himself for it.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Lie
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Confronted with both letters, Rosalind pieces together the story: her grandmother chose respectability over Elias and let him believe indifference. Her grief curdles into anger — at her grandmother, and at herself for repeating the pattern of hiding. Emotional beat: betrayal and recognition; the past is a mirror, not a window.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The ferry company announces the final crossing before winter layup — the same day the house sale closes. Theo, burned by watching Elias lose everything to silence, asks Rosalind plainly to choose: stay, or leave with the letter unanswered like everyone before them. Emotional beat: the ultimatum neither wants; stakes become personal and immediate.

chapters.title: Coda in D Minor
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At the last crossing, townsfolk gather for the traditional end-of-season concert. Rosalind, terrified, borrows a battered cello from the ferry office and plays the piece she failed years ago — finishing it this time, shaking, seen by everyone including Theo. Emotional beat: climax; the broken performance finally completed, identity reclaimed in public.

chapters.title: Out of Season
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, closing with a shared scene. She mails both letters — grandmother's and Elias's — to Theo's family archive, sells the house to a young musician instead of a developer, and stays through winter. In the epilogue beat, the garden blooms early under their care. Emotional beat: resolution; belonging chosen deliberately, timing forgiven at last.
